(prod. Scro & Julia Wolf)
(DOG HOUSE)
Notes: Original demo for "DOG HOUSE" by Julia Wolf that was given to Drake. Julia revealed in an interview on the Zach Sang Show on October 27, 2025, that Drake had originally asked her to send him some of her demos, so she began to record over Scro loops. She came up with what ended up becoming "DOG HOUSE," which was originally a longer song, which Drake ended up taking the ending chorus to use for the final track. Drake resonated with it, and Julia did not end up hearing it again until much later. Julia Wolf later fully previewed her vocals from the demo in a TikTok captioned "chew me up and spit me outtttt!!" on November 6, 2025. Era unconfirmed.

The song was first previewed on September 6, 2021, by a DJ in a bowling alley, then on April 7, 2023 it was played on Drake's OVO Sirius XM/Sound 42 Radio, but with distortion on parts of the song. Dated August 29th, 2021 at approximately 4:39:20PM. Has a piano outro that would later be reused as the outro to "Knife Talk" from the released version of Certified Lover Boy, likely because the song got scrapped.

Name:
⭐ Trance [V3]
(feat. Travis Scott & Young Thug) (prod. Metro Boomin & Allen Ritter)
Notes:
OG Filename: Trance V2 Mix Master 6.9.22 44 16
Track 7 on an early tracklist for Honestly, Nevermind including a scrapped Drake verse. Metro Boomin claimed Drake was cut due to the song already being complete, but it was later revealed that he had wanted the song for his own album 'Honestly, Nevermind', and it appears on tracklist art he released on his 100 GIGS site. Supposedly this is the song Drake had badgered Metro about sending him shortly after his mother had passed, leading to their falling out. Metro's mother was killed just a month after this master was made, and Honestly, Nevermind released two weeks afterward. This is presumably the real reason Metro ultimately refused to give the song to Drake and cut him off his album's version. This situation was rumored during the Kendrick beef in 2024, but eventually confirmed by Thug in leaked jail calls in 2025. This version features different mixing, alternate production, shorter Thug verse and also lacks Peter Lee Johnson’s violin throughout the song.

Name:
Clipse - Showing Out (Remix)
(feat. Drake) (prod. The Neptunes)
Notes: At a Sony media event on July 20th, 2009, the Clipse (Pusha T & Malice) revealed info about their then-forthcoming third studio album (fourth overall) 'Till The Casket Drops'. The revealed outside production from frequent production duo The Neptunes (Pharrell Williams & Chad Hugo) as well as the album's features, which included Drake. The album would drop without Drake's feature (with Yo Gotti replacing track on the track), though it would be played at the Playboy Mansion around the first week of 2010 (it was noted to be a remix, even though Drake's verse was recorded before Yo Gotti's). The reason for its removal can be presumed to be Drake's further alignment with YMCMB (to which Wayne and Birdman had their past issues with Clipse), and his subsequent removal from a tour which had N.E.R.D & Clipse as headliners (he would ironically be replaced by his YMCMB labelmate Tyga).
